did_you_know.text: Did you know? Ezekiel’s vision takes place while he is among the exiles by the Kebar River. During the vision, the heavens open and he sees visions of God.
Did you know? The revelation is dated to the fifth year of King Jehoiachin’s exile, on the fifth day of the fourth month.
Did you know? Ezekiel is identified as the son of Buzi the priest, and the vision takes place in the land of the Chaldeans, by the Kebar River. There the hand of the Lord was upon him.
Did you know? The vision begins with a storm wind coming from the north, a great cloud, flashing fire, and radiance surrounding it. From within the fire appeared something like glowing amber.
Did you know? Each of the four living creatures is described as having four faces and four wings.
Did you know? The four living creatures have four kinds of faces: the face of a human being, a lion, an ox, and an eagle.
Did you know? The living creatures are described as burning coals and flaming torches, with lightning and radiance emerging from the fire.
Did you know? Beside each of the four living creatures there is a wheel, positioned on the ground next to it.
Did you know? The rims of the wheels are described as tall and full of eyes all around, emphasizing their wondrous and terrifying appearance.

Did you know? Above the expanse appeared something resembling a throne, like sapphire stone, with a figure resembling a human being seated upon it. At the end, the appearance is described as the likeness of the glory of the Lord, and Ezekiel falls facedown.
